ranking.name: Qwen3.6-35B-A3B
ranking.runtime: llama.cpp server in Docker, ghcr.io/ggml-org/llama.cpp:server-cuda-b12407 (CUDA 12.8.1; server-cuda13 is likely refused on GeForce by NVIDIA_REQUIRE_CUDA cuda>=13.5, and no b12418 image tag exists). Flags: --jinja, -c 131072, -fa on, -np 1, --n-cpu-moe 21-22 (or leave it out and let --fit place experts), --no-mmproj. Add -e GGML_CUDA_DISABLE_GRAPHS=1 if the laptop GPU hangs (#27330). Ollama qwen3.6:35b-a3b with OLLAMA_CONTEXT_LENGTH=65536 is the simpler fallback. vLLM is not viable: the smallest checkpoint is 19.4 GiB and UVA expert offload is broken by #66264.
ranking.reason: This is the strongest agentic coder in the set that runs at interactive speed with modest offload. NVIDIA's same-harness table gives SWE-bench Verified 70.12 and Terminal-Bench 2.1 44.38, which is independent of Qwen and still ahead of Gemma 4 26B-A4B (57.4 / 37.2) and gpt-oss-20b (52.4 / 15.2). Qwen's own scores are SWE-V 73.4 and TB2.0 51.5, and Qwen ran SkillsBench through OpenCode itself. The layout is cheap on memory: 10 of 40 layers are full attention, so KV is 20 KiB/token and 131k context fits. Only about 9 GiB of experts sit in RAM, and with 3B active the decode estimate is 40-90 tok/s (inferred, not measured). Tool calls use native Qwen3-Coder XML, which llama.cpp routes to its dedicated parser. Corrections applied: the planned 14.0-14.5 GiB GPU load leaves only 0.3-0.8 GiB of headroom, so use --n-cpu-moe 21-22 rather than 20. Sampling: general thinking is temp 1.0 with presence_penalty 1.5, precise coding is temp 0.6 with presence 0. Risks: llama.cpp #30118 can leak a tool call into content when the opener is missing, the laptop CUDA-graph hang #27330 can occur, and thinking is on by default.

ranking.name: gpt-oss-20b
ranking.runtime: llama.cpp server-cuda-b12407 with -hf ggml-org/gpt-oss-20b-GGUF:MXFP4, -c 131072, -ctk/-ctv q8_0, -fa on, -np 1, --jinja, fully on GPU. Second choice is vLLM v0.33.0 with --gpu-memory-utilization 0.95, --kv-cache-dtype fp8, --max-model-len 65536, --attention-backend TRITON_ATTN (TRITON_ATTN supports both sinks and FP8 KV on sm_120, and it works around #61239), --tool-call-parser openai, --reasoning-parser openai_gptoss and --reasoning-effort-map. Use the Python frontend.
ranking.checkpoint: ggml-org/gpt-oss-20b-GGUF MXFP4 (11.28 GiB) for llama.cpp; openai/gpt-oss-20b (12.82 GiB) for vLLM
ranking.reason: This is the most practical candidate. The official checkpoint fits entirely on the GPU in both vLLM and llama.cpp. vLLM v0.33.0 has an explicit sm_120 path in source (MXFP4 MoE goes to MARLIN). It also has the only measured speed in the study: 204.85 tok/s tg128 on a desktop RTX 5080, and the laptop part has 7% less bandwidth. llama.cpp holds the full 128k context in about 13.9 GiB. Agentic quality is middling on independent measures (NVIDIA harness: SWE-V 52.44, TB2.1 15.17), and every higher number for it is OpenAI's own. Thinking is always on, with only low, medium or high effort. Open Harmony and tool bugs: vLLM #65770 (HTTP 500 after a malformed tool name), #58825, and llama.cpp #30781 (HTTP 500 for an array parameter without items, which OpenCode MCP tools could hit). The vLLM KV pool is tight: about 48k tokens at BF16, so FP8 KV and 0.95 are needed to reach 64k.

ranking.name: Qwen3.8-27B
ranking.runtime: llama.cpp server-cuda-b12407, fully on GPU: -ngl all, --no-mmproj, -c 65536, -ctk/-ctv q8_0, -fa on, -np 1, --jinja. Set -e GGML_CUDA_DISABLE_GRAPHS=1, because #27330 was reproduced on driver 595.99.02 under Ubuntu 26.04. vLLM does not fit: even the smallest AutoRound build (15.59 GiB) exceeds the budget. Ollama qwen3.8:27b (18 GB) spills onto the CPU.
ranking.reason: This has the highest agentic ceiling of any model that fits fully in 16 GB. Artificial Analysis measured Terminal-Bench 2.1 at 79.8% (xhigh) and 65.2% (medium) independently, while the vendor reports SWE-bench Pro 61.7, but Terminal-Bench 4.0 is only 5.6%. It ranks below #1 and #2 for practical reasons. It runs only at 3-bit, and the quality loss is unmeasured. Context tops out around 64-88k. Dense decode is bounded at about 40-45 tok/s (inferred). The q8_0 KV speed penalty is still contested (PR #31802 open). Hybrid-model prefix-cache misses (#30357) can force a full re-prefill on long agent turns. Use reasoning_effort medium; the default is xhigh.

ranking.name: Gemma 4 26B-A4B IT
ranking.runtime: llama.cpp server-cuda-b12407, text-only (no mmproj), -ngl 99, -c 65536, -ctk/-ctv q8_0, -fa on, -np 1, --jinja, temp 1.0, top_p 0.95, top_k 64. For more context, add --n-cpu-moe 6-9. vLLM does not fit at 0.92 (about 11.8k context).
ranking.reason: It runs fully on the GPU at 64k with q8_0 KV, using an official Google QAT checkpoint. NVIDIA's same-harness table gives SWE-V 57.4 and TB2.1 37.2, clearly ahead of gpt-oss-20b, and with 3.8B active it should be fast. Corrections applied: the KV headroom figure was a subtraction error, so F16 KV at 64k does not fit and q8_0 is mandatory (it fits about 79-129k). Plan B at 256k needs about --n-cpu-moe 9. Other sources disagree on its agentic strength: Qwen's scaffold measured SWE-V 17.4 and KAT measured 35.8. Open llama.cpp #29655 reports unstable streaming write and edit arguments for this model, which matters for OpenCode's edit tool. Thinking is off by default.

ranking.name: Ornith-1.5-9B
ranking.runtime: vLLM v0.33.0 (vllm/vllm-openai:v0.33.0), fully on GPU, Python frontend: --language-model-only, --max-model-len 262144 (or 131072), --kv-cache-dtype fp8, --enable-auto-tool-choice, --tool-call-parser qwen3_coder, --reasoning-parser qwen3. FP8 KV routes attention to FlashInfer or Triton, not FA2. Keep --enforce-eager in reserve for the sm_120 hybrid-GDN NVFP4 instability (#54331). The alternative is llama.cpp with the Q8_0 GGUF at 262k and q8_0 KV (about 14.4 GiB).
ranking.reason: This has the cleanest vLLM-on-sm_120 setup in the set. The checkpoint is W4A16 NVFP4, and on capability 120 v0.33.0 forces Marlin, so there is no FlashInfer FP4 JIT and no 52 GiB host-RAM spike. It runs fully on the GPU with the full 262k context at FP8 KV, uses Qwen3-Coder XML tools and has a thinking toggle. Decode ceiling is about 166 tok/s (inferred). The rank rests only on vendor claims: SWE-V 70.6 and TB2.1 46.2 are self-reported by an unverified org, the linked LICENSE returns 404, and no independent result exists. The template reads reasoning_content while vLLM emits 'reasoning', so interleaved thinking may be dropped across OpenCode turns.

ranking.name: Gemma 4 12B IT
ranking.runtime: vLLM v0.33.0, fully on GPU: --tool-call-parser gemma4, --reasoning-parser gemma4, --enable-auto-tool-choice, the image/audio mm limits set to 0, --max-model-len 131072, --max-num-seqs 1-2. Add --kv-cache-dtype fp8 for headroom; attention is forced to TRITON_ATTN, which accepts FP8 KV. The alternative is llama.cpp server-cuda-b12407 with the official QAT Q4_0 (about 10 GiB VRAM at 128k).
ranking.checkpoint: google/gemma-4-12B-it-qat-w4a16-ct (9.56 GiB, official Google QAT, Marlin path on sm_120)
ranking.reason: An official vendor 4-bit checkpoint on a source-verified Marlin kernel path, fully on the GPU at 128k or more. Setup is simple and needs no JIT. It is the most dependable Gemma-family vLLM option. Correction applied: v0.33.0 async scheduling reserves 2x2048 in-flight tokens for sliding-window KV, so the BF16 maximum is lower than the 193k first claimed. 131072 in BF16 is now tight, and FP8 KV makes it comfortable. Independent AA results are modest (TB2.1 27.3%, TB-Hard 18.2%, tau2-telecom 36.3%), and Google publishes no SWE or Terminal scores. Open gemma4 parser bugs affect agent loops: #54256 (dropped tool calls), #66430 and #50889.

ranking.name: Qwen3.5-9B
ranking.runtime: vLLM v0.33.0, fully on GPU: --language-model-only, -e MAX_JOBS=2, --linear-backend cutlass (or accept the FlashInfer CUTLASS JIT with MAX_JOBS=2), --max-model-len 131072, --tool-call-parser qwen3_coder, --reasoning-parser qwen3, --enable-auto-tool-choice. The alternative is llama.cpp server-cuda-b12407 with unsloth Q8_0 at 131k.
ranking.checkpoint: RedHatAI/Qwen3.5-9B-NVFP4 (7.42 GiB language-only); llama.cpp unsloth/Qwen3.5-9B-GGUF Q8_0
ranking.reason: The official base of Ornith and MiMo, and it fits fully on the GPU at 131-262k with native Qwen3-Coder XML tools. Its coding-agent scores come only from other vendors' harnesses, not Qwen's own: SWE-V 53.2 (Ornith's OpenHands run) and TB2.1 19-27. Ranked below Ornith and Gemma 12B because its NVFP4 W4A4 path goes through FlashInfer CUTLASS on sm_120. That path has the JIT host-RAM issue (#46268) and no sm_120 validation for this checkpoint, and the checkpoint is a third-party quant. Open qwen3_coder streaming bug #65774.

ranking.name: NVIDIA Nemotron 3.5 Lightning 30B-A3B
ranking.runtime: llama.cpp server-cuda-b12407: -ngl 99, --n-cpu-moe 16, -c 131072 (262144 with q8_0 KV), -fa on, -np 1, --jinja, temp 1.0, top_p 0.95. Do not rely on force_nonempty_content in llama.cpp: the challenge found it is a no-op there. vLLM is not viable on this GPU because of #66264 with marlin NVFP4 offload.
ranking.reason: The best NVIDIA-family option for coding on this machine. It needs only about 5.5 GiB of experts in RAM (7 of 23 MoE layers). KV costs just 6 KiB/token because there are only 6 attention layers, so 128-256k context is cheap. Tool calls use Qwen3-Coder XML, which llama.cpp auto-detects. On NVIDIA's own harness it is mid-tier: SWE-V 51.56 and TB2.1 24.58, about level with gpt-oss-20b and well below Qwen3.6-35B-A3B. NVIDIA positions it for speed and tool-use reliability. Thinking is on by default.

ranking.name: GLM-4.7-Flash
ranking.runtime: llama.cpp server-cuda-b12407: -ngl 99, --n-cpu-moe 19-20 (corrected: layer 0 is dense, so 18 is borderline), -c 65536, -fa on, --jinja, temp 0.7, top_p 1.0. -ctk q8_0 is an option for headroom (crash issue #19724 was closed). Ollama glm-4.7-flash with num_ctx 65536 is the fallback. The vLLM INT4 plus UVA offload route is refuted by #66264.
ranking.reason: A strong 30B-A3B thinking coder with an MIT license and native GLM XML tool calls. The llama.cpp template is byte-identical to the HF one and covered by tests. Vendor numbers are SWE-V 59.2 and tau2 79.5; the independent AA results are lower (TB-Hard 22%, GPQA 58 against the vendor's 75). It is lower than Lightning on practicality: it puts about 6 GiB of experts in RAM at 64k, and MLA KV is 54 KiB/token, so going past 64k costs more offload. The vLLM glm47 parser has several open bugs (#67684, #60703, #67471), which is why llama.cpp is the runtime.

ranking.name: Qwen3-Coder-30B-A3B-Instruct
ranking.runtime: llama.cpp server-cuda-b12407: -ngl 99, --n-cpu-moe 17, -c 65536, -ctk/-ctv q8_0, -fa on, --jinja, temp 0.7, top_p 0.8, top_k 20, repeat-penalty 1.05. Use --n-cpu-moe 27 for 128k. The vLLM AWQ plus UVA offload route is refuted by #66264.
ranking.reason: The no-thinking pick with dedicated tool calling. It never produces think blocks, so it avoids OpenCode #55378 (empty reasoning-only turns), and it uses the dedicated Qwen3-Coder PEG parser. About 5.6 GiB of experts go to RAM at 64k. It is older (2025-07-31, outside the window), and an independent same-harness run (Kwaipilot) gave only SWE-V 31.8 and TB2.1 13.5, against the vendor's 51.6. It is included because the user asked for a no-thinking model listed separately and this is the most practical one with tools. Qwen3.6-35B-A3B with enable_thinking=false is the stronger no-thinking alternative.

notes:
I judged from the supplied records and did not browse.

Cross-cutting corrections I applied:
1. Use llama.cpp image ghcr.io/ggml-org/llama.cpp:server-cuda-b12407 (CUDA 12.8.1, native sm_120a SASS). Do not use server-cuda13: its NVIDIA_REQUIRE_CUDA cuda>=13.5 has no GeForce brand clause, so it is likely refused on this host (inferred). The server-cuda13-b12418 tag returns 404.
2. vLLM UVA expert offload (--cpu-offload-gb with --cpu-offload-params experts) is undone for Marlin-repacked MoE weights in v0.33.0 (#66264). That refutes every vLLM offload plan: Qwen3-Coder-30B AWQ, GLM INT4, Lightning NVFP4, Laguna NVFP4, Qwen3.6 NVFP4. MoE models above 16 GB therefore rank on llama.cpp only.
3. FP8 KV on sm_120 bypasses FA2 and goes to FlashInfer or Triton. For gpt-oss, set --attention-backend TRITON_ATTN. For Mistral3, TRITON_ATTN is mandatory (#53481).
4. The NVIDIA Container Toolkit must be installed first. CDI injection (--device nvidia.com/gpu=all) is preferred on this systemd-cgroup host. heavy does not cap containers, so set --memory and --memory-swap on each one.
5. Whichever runtime is used, OpenCode v2.3.0 needs capabilities.tools=true and an explicit limit.context. OpenCode #60202 does not bite on stock vLLM v0.33.0.

Thinking and tool calling, by rank:
- Toggle thinking, with tools: Qwen3.6-35B-A3B, Qwen3.8-27B, Gemma 4 26B-A4B, Ornith-1.5-9B, Gemma 4 12B, Qwen3.5-9B, Nemotron 3.5 Lightning, GLM-4.7-Flash.
- Always thinking, with tools: gpt-oss-20b.
- No thinking, with tools: Qwen3-Coder-30B-A3B-Instruct. Outside the top 10: Qwen3-Coder-Next, Devstral Small 2 24B, and the Ministral 3 Instruct variants.
- Thinking, no tools: DeepSeek-R1-0528-Qwen3-8B (unsuitable for OpenCode).

Excluded, and why:
- Qwen3-Coder-Next: strongest non-thinking model (AA TB2.1 38.2%, tau2 79.5%), but it needs 25.7 GiB of experts in RAM out of about 40 GiB free. The UD-IQ4_XS quant also risks the sm_120 IQ-quant miscompile (#28581) on CUDA 13.2.x builds.
- KAT-Coder-V2.5-Dev: about 8.3 GiB in RAM. Its benchmarks are contested against its own base, Qwen3.6-35B-A3B, and there is no official quant, so Qwen3.6 dominates it.
- Laguna XS 2.1: self-reported scores trail Qwen3.6 on every benchmark in its own vendor table.
- MiMo-V2.6-Distill-Qwen-9B: only +1.1 SWE-V over its base, and the tool-argument format is contested between the vLLM parser and the ggml-org patched template.
- Granite 4.2 8B: weak independent scores (AA Intelligence Index 5.1). The MXFP4 build has a cute-dsl crash risk on sm_120.
- Ministral 3: AA TB2.1 9.7% / 4.1%. On vLLM the 14B needs 0.95 for 64k.
- Nemotron 3 Nano 4B, Nemotron 3.5 Bolt E4B, Gemma 4 E4B: small edge models that fit easily but have no coding-agent evidence. Bolt's context is capped at exactly 65,536. These are useful only as title, compaction or sub-agent models.
- Devstral Small 2: dense 24B, which reaches only about 32k with q8_0 KV (64k needs q4_0 KV).
- gpt-oss-120b: about 49-52 GiB of experts in RAM against about 40 GiB free.

Placements that rest only on vendor claims: Ornith-1.5-9B (#5) entirely. Qwen3.8-27B is partly backed by Artificial Analysis (TB2.1 independent), and Qwen3.6-35B-A3B is backed by NVIDIA's same-harness numbers.

Gaps:
- No candidate has been run end to end with OpenCode.
- The only measured speed figure is for gpt-oss-20b, and it was on a desktop RTX 5080, not this laptop GPU.
- Offload throughput depends on DDR5 bandwidth, which is unmeasured on this machine.
